ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=2b8ccac18a70 (bumping swoosh) included a change to email-service/internal/attachment/buffer.go and email-service/internal/sender/send.go that introduced a retain() call on attachment byte slices inside SendWithAttachments() without a corresponding release() after SMTP transmission completes. As a result, every attachment buffer allocated per email send is held indefinitely in the sender's internal reference map, preventing the Go garbage collector from reclaiming the memory. Under normal send volume (~50-100 emails/min with multi-MB attachments), this causes unbounded heap growth (observed: ~250MB/min), leading to repeated OOMKill cycles (3 within 30 minutes). The stack trace consistently points to email-service/internal/attachment.(*Buffer).retain() called from email-service/internal/sender.SendWithAttachments().
ground_truth_remediation: 1. IMMEDIATE: Rolling-restart email-service pods to temporarily recover memory headroom (buys ~5-10 minutes per pod before leak re-accumulates). 2. Scale email-service horizontally to 4+ replicas and enable rate limiting to reduce per-pod send throughput while fix is prepared. 3. CODE FIX (within 2 hours): In email-service/internal/sender/send.go, add a deferred buf.Release() call immediately after buf.Retain() inside SendWithAttachments() so that each attachment buffer is freed upon function return regardless of send outcome. 4. Deploy the patched build and verify heap_alloc stabilizes below 200MB under normal load. 5. Add a unit test asserting that Buffer.refCount returns to 0 after SendWithAttachments completes to prevent regression.
